Subject: Dedicated Capacity: Traffic Census & Prompt/Response Sampling for ZephyrAI Deal

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. To get Marissa and the pre-sales sizing team a clear starting point for the Dedicated capacity proposal, could you share a short traffic census and a handful of representative prompt/response samples? Specifically we need: 

- A small CSV with 2–4 representative workloads (API route name, average qps, peak qps, typical concurrency, p50/p95 response token length, p50/p95 prompt token length, session duration). A single-day sample is fine.
- 6–10 example prompt/response pairs (sanitized) across high-cost and low-cost flows — include user/session annotations if available.
- Expected burst / daypart windows (local time) and any compliance/regulatory constraints (e.g., cannot leave tokens in cache beyond X hours).

I've attached a tiny template you can drop numbers into (redwood_precommit_workbook_v1.xlsx) and pasted a Drive link in case that's easier. Vivek is cc'd for any low-level telemetry questions.

Goal: With that info Marissa will produce a first-pass GPU mix and reserved capacity projection we can review next week. If you can get the CSV and a few samples to me by EOD Friday (Dec 4) that would keep our timeline intact.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198 | tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_precommit_workbook_v1.xlsx

Hi Tessa —

Thanks — attaching a one-day export we pulled from our staging cluster: zephyr_traffic_sample.csv. It contains three routes: "ingest_text", "summarize_api", and "agent_prompt". We've sanitized PII. Quick notes:

- avg qps is low for ingest_text (0.4) but spikes to ~75 qps on weekday billing runs.
- summarize_api is steady during business hours, p95 response length ~820 tokens.
- agent_prompt is chat-like; sessions average ~9 minutes, median concurrency per session ~2.

I'll drop a separate email with 8 example prompt/response pairs as requested. Let me know if the CSV layout needs adjustments for Marissa.

Best,
Aisha

Perfect — thanks for sending the CSV. A few clarifying Qs before Marissa begins sizing: 

1) For the summarize_api p95 at ~820 response tokens, can you confirm the model family (Llama 2.2 / GPT-4-equivalent / etc.) and whether responses are streamed or buffered today?
2) For agent_prompt: are messages single-turn or multi-turn sessions where the KV cache length grows? If multi-turn, what is the average number of messages per session and the typical max sequence length you observe?
3) Do you have an expected monthly growth percentage for QPS? If you have a simple month-on-month growth number we can produce a 12-month reserve plan.

I've pasted a tiny example below of how we map prompt/response lengths to token compute costs for our sizing (helps Marissa pick quantization and GPU mix).

— example mapping —
route: summarize_api | p50 prompt 120 tokens | p95 response 820 tokens | typical concurrency 1.2 | session duration 14s

If you want, Marissa can run a quick "first pass" with the attached workbook and then we'll do an internal review before sending the GPU mix.

Thanks,
Tessa

Thanks for the sample, Aisha — I ran a quick first-pass into the precommit workbook and attached my export (redwood_precommit_workbook_v1.xlsx). High-level notes from our sizing probe: 

- Baseline footprint: With current traffic and p95 sizes, a modest Dedicated pool of 8 A100-class GPUs (or 12x L4-class in GPU-hybrid mix with quantization) would cover steady-state plus expected bursts with our default autoscaling/bursting policy.
- Burst handling: ingest_text spike to 75 qps is the dominant tail event — recommend a spike-burst policy that leverages transient burst capacity (2–4 GPUs) for the 20–30 minute weekday runs rather than permanently committing.
- KV cache: if agent_prompt sessions hold long multi-turn contexts (9min with 8–12 messages), we should reserve additional memory headroom per-GPU for KV storage; please confirm average max sequence length for agent_prompt.

Next steps: Aisha — if you can forward the sanitized prompt/response pairs and a one-week window of hourly qps we can do a short Monte Carlo run to stress-test the proposed pool and give a probability of p99 latency violation under the current autoscale settings.

I can present the detailed workbook and GPU-mix options in a 30-minute walkthrough; propose Wed, Dec 9 10:00am PT. Thoughts?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Pre-Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Could you include a short appendix in the workbook showing the cost delta between A100-only and L4-hybrid options (1/3/6-month commitment scenarios)? That'll help our finance team.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Aisha
